title: Talbot Place the spirit of Ibsen would blow through him like a keen wind, a spirit of wayward boyish beauty;
html_source: Henrik Ibsen (1828-1906), the great Norwegian dramatists, one of Joyce’s mentors. Joyce wrote an essay on Ibsen’s drama in 1900 and remarked that, in When We Dead Awaken, the sculptor Rubek’s wife (awakened from her spiritual death) is ‘as a breath of keen air’. This may be the association with the stonecutter’s works. But part of the meaning of this programmed journey to the university, with all its attendant associations, is its privacy. Stephen is creating an imaginative world that runs parallel to the actual world he inhabits.
